title: Letter and Orchard
premise: In the port town of Iloran, Vesper Okonkwo has survived a decade of indenture to the Meridian Trading Company by mastering silence—until the army arrives, seizes the town, and confiscates the ledger holding every diver's debt and death record. When Vesper learns the victors plan to burn the ledger and rewrite the company's history as benevolent, he races to copy its pages with help from an orchard-keeping widow, a disgraced clerk, and the children of drowned divers. The climax comes as soldiers torch the counting house while Vesper smuggles the copied ledger out in a coffin of orchard fruit; the book ends years later, when his testimony forces the victors' historians to print the true names, and Vesper, freed, plants an orchard over the old counting house.
about_author: Ada Ishikawa is the pen name of a former archivist who spent six years cataloguing colonial trading ledgers before turning to fiction. She writes from a coastal town where pearling history is still contested, and her novels center on the people records leave out.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Vesper Okonkwo dives at dawn for the Meridian Trading Company, counting breaths and debts alike. Through his POV we learn how his father drowned and how silence became survival. He watches the new clerk mark a dead diver 'absconded' rather than 'lost.' Emotional beat: quiet dread—the rules that keep him safe are also erasing him.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Small Silences
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: ten-year-old Vesper is indentured after his mother's death, taken in grudgingly by Mama Sefu, the orchard widow behind the compound wall. His POV braids past and present, showing the found family forming around stolen figs and whispered stories. Beat: warmth discovered inside captivity, and the first lie he tells to protect someone.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Names
chapters.summary: Vesper is sent to the counting house to fetch rope and glimpses the master ledger: columns of debts, deaths, and 'disposals.' Clerk Ilya Petrov, drunk and ashamed, lets him look too long. Vesper's POV; beat: vertigo—he realizes the paper knows more truth than any mouth in Iloran dares speak.

chapters.title: Gunboats at First Light
chapters.summary: The army arrives without warning, requisitioning the harbor, the warehouses, and the company itself under a victors' charter. POV shifts to Sergeant Amara Diallo, a conscript officer uneasy about her orders. Beat: the town holds its breath; Vesper recognizes that occupation changes who must be silent about what.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Soldiers inventory everything—including the ledger, now sealed as 'evidence pending historical review.' Vesper watches it carried past him like a body. His POV; beat: cold clarity. The document containing his father's real fate now belongs to men who will decide what it meant.

chapters.title: The Historian's Pen
chapters.summary: Victors' historian Edouard Marchand arrives to write the official account, interviewing townsfolk coached by company men. Vesper is summoned as a 'native witness' and gives careful, empty answers. Alternating POV with Marchand, who privately doubts his sources. Beat: Vesper sees the machinery of myth-making begin to turn.

chapters.title: What Ilya Knew
chapters.summary: Vesper finds Ilya hiding in the fish market, dismissed and half-starved. Ilya confesses the ledger's second column—payments made to keep divers' families quiet—and admits he kept carbon copies once, then burned them out of fear. Ilya's POV. Beat: guilt offered like a wound; Vesper decides someone must get the truth on record.

chapters.title: Figs and Ash
chapters.summary: Vesper brings Ilya to Mama Sefu's orchard, where the three form an unlikely conspiracy. They learn the army plans to burn the counting house archives 'for sanitation' within weeks. Mama Sefu's POV. Beat: resolve hardening into plan—an old woman offers her cellar, her fruit crates, and her fury.

chapters.title: Children of Drowned Men
chapters.summary: Vesper recruits other indentured divers' children, each of whom can recite fragments of the ledger from memory: debts, dates, the names struck through. Group scene, mostly Vesper's POV with interludes. Beat: grief becoming purpose—a found family becomes a living archive.

chapters.title: The Copying Nights
chapters.summary: By lamplight in the cellar, the conspirators transcribe what they remember while Ilya reconstructs figures from habit. A near-discovery when a patrol knocks; Mama Sefu covers with a story about preserving fruit. Vesper's POV. Beat: terror and tenderness intertwined—the work feels like prayer.

chapters.title: Marchand's Doubt
chapters.summary: Marchand interviews Sergeant Diallo, who slips him an unofficial casualty count that contradicts the company's numbers. His POV reveals his crisis: career or conscience. Beat: the enemy's historian begins leaning toward the truth, though Vesper cannot know it yet.

chapters.title: A Name Struck Through
chapters.summary: The memory-circle reaches Vesper's father's entry: not 'lost at sea' but 'debt settled by estate seizure'—the company took their home the week he drowned. Vesper breaks; Mama Sefu holds him. His POV. Beat: rage and release; the personal cost of the record becomes undeniable.

chapters.title: Diallo's Choice
chapters.summary: Ordered to escort the archive wagons to the burning ground early, Diallo delays by falsifying a transport manifest, buying days. Her POV. Beat: complicity inverted—one soldier quietly joins the resistance she doesn't fully understand.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Market
chapters.summary: A memory-circle boy is caught reciting figures to a fishmonger and interrogated; he gives up nothing but the circle must scatter. Vesper suspects Ilya was followed. Tense ensemble scene, Vesper's POV. Beat: fear fracturing trust at the worst moment.

chapters.title: The Confession of Ilya Petrov
chapters.summary: Ilya, certain he'll be arrested, writes a full signed confession naming the company's payments and deaths, entrusting it to Vesper. His POV, elegiac. Beat: redemption through paper—a coward's final act of courage.

chapters.title: The Burning Order
chapters.summary: The army moves the fire date up; the counting house will burn in three days. Marchand, tipped off by Diallo, secretly warns Mama Sefu via a market note. Alternating POV. Beat: the clock collapses; the plan must happen now, imperfectly.

chapters.title: Coffin of Fruit
chapters.summary: The conspirators hide the copied ledger, Ilya's confession, and sworn name-lists inside false-bottomed fruit crates bound for a funeral procession—Mama Sefu burying an old friend. Soldiers inspect the cortege and wave it through. Vesper's POV, white-knuckle suspense. Beat: the dead carry the living's truth out of the flames.

chapters.title: Fire at the Counting House
chapters.summary: The original ledger burns publicly as Marchand watches, ordered to record only the official narrative. But Diallo passes him a scrap: one true page. His POV. Beat: climax of conscience—the historian chooses which fire to feed.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Vesper walks into Marchand's office uninvited and lays the copied ledger on his desk, speaking the names aloud for hours while Diallo guards the door. Marchand's POV as he abandons the sanctioned draft. Beat: catharsis—ten years of silence broken in a single room.

chapters.title: The Reckoning of Names
chapters.summary: Marchand publishes the true account with appendices of names; the company's charter is revoked and surviving families receive restitution hearings. Ilya testifies and is imprisoned briefly, then pardoned. Ensemble resolution. Beat: justice arriving incomplete but real.

chapters.title: Indenture's End
chapters.summary: Vesper's contract is voided; he is legally free and discovers freedom feels strangely weightless. He buries his father's restored name-marker beside Mama Sefu's orchard wall. His POV. Beat: mourning finally permitted—the silence lifted, not just ended.

chapters.title: Letter and Orchard
chapters.summary: Years later, Vesper plants an orchard over the ruined counting house and teaches the memory-circle children to read from the printed ledger. A letter arrives from Marchand enclosing Diallo's commendation. Final image: young trees where debt was counted. Beat: inheritance transformed—from ledgers of loss to roots that bear fruit.
